CANOPY / FIELD GUIDE

The conclusion is
only half the experiment.

Canopy asks whether several independently named devices show a similar change after accounting for their own activity baselines. It is an experimental signal-analysis tool, not a medical product.

  1. Learn a baseline. Fit heart rate against activity for each device using the first 120 seconds. Use a robust residual scale with a 3 bpm floor.
  2. Collect witnesses. In each 50 m cell and 30 second window, take the median standardized residual per eligible device. At least two samples per device are required.
  3. Apply quorum. At least three eligible devices and 60% above a residual score of 3 create a shared-change flag. This score is a heuristic, not a calibrated probability.
  4. Challenge it. Remove each device in turn. A flag is labeled robust only if every removal preserves quorum. This checks dependence on one device; it does not prove device independence.
  5. Inspect context. Ambient-temperature change is evidence to investigate. It is not used to claim causality, diagnose strain, or estimate core temperature.

Try to break it

Compare activity-only and single-sensor cases with the shared event. Then choose “All sensors drift together”: the detector flags a shared change despite no ambient shift. This is an intentional counterexample, not a solved case. Boundary splitting and missing packets can also conceal real events.

Your own capsule

Open JSON with schema canopy/1 and a samples array. Every sample needs device, seq, t_s, x_m, y_m, hr_bpm, activity (0–1), ambient_c, and quality (0–1). Use pseudonymous device IDs and local coordinates. The browser supports up to 50,000 samples and 10 MiB; the local CLI supports 500,000 samples. Start each recording with a representative baseline. Clock resets require a separate session.

What is actually validated?

Software invariants and deliberately simple synthetic cases. No physical devices, medical outcomes, real-world false-alarm rates, or network independence have been validated. Workload regression can be confounded; the synthetic benchmark is not clinical evidence. Figma editing was unavailable due to the existing account quota; this interface is implemented directly in HTML and CSS.

Exports contain the input dataset, settings, algorithm version, and report. Replay recomputes the report from the input; imported report text is never trusted. Sharing exports shares any data you include.
